notes.detail: Was '{exactText} درست · {relatedText} متعلقہ': 'درست' means correct/right, so the pair sat on two axes (quality vs relatedness) and the line's only job - the exact/related split - was blurred. Now 'مطابق: {exactText} · متعلقہ: {relatedText}'. Both tiers are now on the match axis, the 'correct' misreading is gone, and the label shares its root with the noun count.match already uses ('مطابقت'), so the overlay's vocabulary is consistent. Residual, not a defect: 'مطابق' reads as 'matching' rather than the emphatic 'عین مطابق'; the contrast with 'متعلقہ' carries 'exact', so no change asked for.

The label is unchanged at the new bytes (canonical files are byte-identical to round 1), so nothing was addressed in code. My finding was conditional on the control's room ('keep as is if it fits'), so leaving it stands as the answered disposition; it was non-blocking and remains an observation for the next wave, not a defect.

Unchanged ('کسی دوسرے ڈیوائس پر'). My NIT was itself conditional on how the shipped ur copy treats ڈیوائس elsewhere ('otherwise no change'); the masculine oblique is attested Urdu, so no edit is required and none was made.

The English sidecar now states the label-first rule and why a numeral next to an agreeing adjective is unsatisfiable; the ur value obeys '{label}: {number}', the middot and both placeholders, so a future wave cannot drift back into the round-1 form without contradicting its own sidecar.
